title: Cut the archive job by bytes, not by files

blocks.text: The nightly archive job compresses the day's uploads on a `ForkJoinPool`. Compressing a file takes time in proportion to its bytes, and the files range from a few bytes to several gigabytes. The job used to cut the list of files in half by count until a batch held a handful of files, and one worker ended up with the batch of video files while the others had finished long before.
`ArchiveJob` now gives each task a budget in bytes. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/ArchiveJob.java`:

items: `isLeaf(from, to)`: whether one task compresses the files `[from, to)`;
`splitPoint(from, to)`: where a batch too big for one task is cut.

blocks.text: When you're done, every batch a task compresses fits the budget, and each cut leaves neither half with more than half the batch's bytes plus the batch's largest file. Some uploads are bigger than the whole budget on their own. `bytesIn(from, to)` is there to use. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: every file is compressed exactly once, in batches that follow each other and fit the budget
a batch is cut where its bytes divide evenly, not where its files do
a batch whose last file holds more than half its bytes is still cut into two non-empty halves
a single file bigger than the budget is compressed as a batch of its own

origin.section: When You Know What Each Item Costs, Split by Cost

concepts: A single item over the budget must be a leaf, and the split point must stay strictly inside the range, or the task splits into itself until the stack overflows.
When item costs are known, a threshold in cost and a split point at half the cost balance the work with few tasks.
